question: A component in one of these libraries owns a piece of interaction state internally and also reports every change to it outward, but it does not accept that state back in: the host can watch the thing open and close, and cannot open or close it. That was invisible for as long as the underlying primitive re-opened itself on the next interaction, and it stops being invisible the moment the primitive stops doing that, because the only code that could reopen it is the host, and the host has no way in. The contract is the one every library here implements for its own state: if a component publishes changes to a piece of state, it must also accept that state as an input and defer to it when it is supplied, so ownership is a choice the host makes rather than one the component makes for it. Elsewhere in the folder the contract is spelled out: one library pairs a state slot with a change handler and an apply helper so the host can hold the collection and feed it back, one lets the host pass any part of the state object and merges it over the internally-managed part, and one warns at runtime when a form element is switched between owning its value and being told it. Which file publishes state it will not accept, and which own the ownership-is-the-host's-choice contract it has to be brought in line with?
